sha_binding.note: 924954c699e4fa00cad61a2c83fa6f8944963ccc is the post-resync merge anchor that includes current main and the substantive lane changes. Every static measurement below was taken on that exact tree in the lane worktree. Subsequent accepted changes are proof or lane-governance metadata, so the execution anchor remains stable. Re-anchored 2026-09-23 after resyncing onto main 4ab51ce86 (merge 4204aa2c2) and incorporating the rewritten race-test commit 25794312c; every measurement below was re-taken on this tree.

what_this_lane_repairs.defect: An evidence-plane settlement could not be corrected. An evidence-plane pick keeps its status (validated / awaiting_approval) after it settles — deliberately, because validated -> settled is not a legal FSM edge — so recordPickSettlement dispatched every LATER operator grade back into recordOperatorEvidenceSettlement rather than to recordSettlementCorrection. The second grade was written as another *original*, corrects_id null, which production's partial unique index settlement_records_pick_source_idx (pick_id, source) WHERE corrects_id IS NULL rejects with 23505.
what_this_lane_repairs.the_second_half_is_worse_than_the_first: The 23505 catch then read back the pre-existing row and RETURNED it as this request's settlementRecord with auditRecords: []. So an operator who regraded a pick from WIN to LOSS received a success response naming a WIN settlement. The refusal was converted into a report that their grade had persisted, when a different grade had. A defect that loses a correction silently is materially worse than one that refuses it.
what_this_lane_repairs.why_the_dispatch_is_not_simply_reordered: Routing evidence-plane picks to recordSettlementCorrection would be wrong in two ways: that function requires the pick to be in 'settled' state (an evidence-plane pick never is) and it writes a same-state lifecycle event, which the evidence plane deliberately does not do. The correction SHAPE is mirrored — read the latest row, link the new one to it, never mutate the old — without adopting the delivery plane's lifecycle behaviour.
what_this_lane_repairs.fail_closed_shape: The 23505 catch is retained as a genuine race guard and now throws ApiError(409, SETTLEMENT_ALREADY_RECORDED) instead of returning someone else's row. The race it guards is real — another writer landing the canonical (pick, source) row between the pre-insert read and this insert — and the correct answer to it is 're-read the current settlement and resubmit', not a fabricated success.
what_this_lane_repairs.no_lifecycle_transition_and_no_delivery: Unchanged by this lane and asserted by it: the operator path still returns lifecycleEvent: null and finalLifecycleState: pick.status, and the WIN -> LOSS -> WIN test counts zero distribution_outbox rows across ALL five statuses after three grades. A correction must not become a route to a member.

unit_tests.label: Three new tests plus the 35 pre-existing ones unchanged. (1) A second operator grade corrects the first: a new row id, corrects_id equal to the first row's id, payload correction:true / priorSettlementRecordId / priorResult:'win', the ORIGINAL read back from the repository still result:'win' with corrects_id null, effectiveSettlement naming the tip at correction_depth 1, and auditActions deepEqual ['settlement.operator_evidence_corrected'] rather than ...graded. (2) WIN -> LOSS -> WIN: at EVERY point in the chain unresolvedReason is null, the effective result is the grade just written, correction_depth equals the position, settlementSummary.total_picks is 1 and total_records is index+1; the three rows read back are [win,null],[loss,id0],[win,id1]; zero outbox rows across all five statuses. (3) A duplicate-key race is refused: the pre-insert read misses and every later read sees the other writer's row, exactly as in the real race, while the insert throws a code-23505 error; and the call rejects with SETTLEMENT_ALREADY_RECORDED while the pre-existing settlement is left untouched.

Full workspace unit suite, run to completion on this tree: 6807 tests, 6807 pass, 0 fail, zero 'not ok' TAP lines, exit 0. The pre-existing assertion deepEqual(auditActions, ['settlement.operator_evidence_graded']) on the FIRST settlement still holds, because the action is renamed only on a correction.

mutation_battery.method: Each mutation applied to apps/api/src/settlement-service.ts alone, the suite run, then the file restored byte-for-byte from a pre-mutation copy. Run with no other suite executing concurrently.

mutations.mutation: Drop `...(isCorrection ? { correctsId: priorSettlement.id } : {})` from the settlements.record() call — i.e. keep the pre-insert read but write the correction as another root.
mutations.expected: The chain breaks into two roots.
mutations.observed: 2 failures — 'a second operator grade corrects the first' and 'WIN -> LOSS -> WIN'. The reported actual value is 'MULTIPLE_ROOT_RECORDS'.
mutations.why_this_is_the_right_discriminator: The in-memory repository does NOT implement the partial unique index, so it never throws 23505 and a mutation test cannot assert on that error here. What it CAN observe is the downstream consequence the index exists to prevent: resolveEffectiveSettlement refuses two root records and returns effectiveSettlement: null. Asserting on MULTIPLE_ROOT_RECORDS is therefore a real discriminator rather than a restatement of the code.

mutations.mutation: Restore main's exact pre-lane 23505 catch body: re-read findLatestForPick and return it as this request's settlementRecord with auditRecords: [].
mutations.expected: The refusal is reported as a success.
mutations.observed: 1 failure — 'a duplicate-key race is refused, never reported as a successful settlement' — because the mutant RESOLVES with the other writer's WIN row. The other 37 pass.
mutations.correction_to_the_earlier_record: Re-running M2 on 2026-09-23 found the earlier race test weaker than recorded: its stub returned null from EVERY findLatestForPick call, so the fake-success branch could never find a row and the mutant failed the test only because the raw 23505 message did not match the expected pattern. Commit 25794312c makes only the pre-insert read miss, so the test now fails the old behaviour for the reason it names. A first 2026-09-23 run of a hand-written M2 that kept the 409 throw after the re-read inverted nothing, which is what exposed this.

static_proof.why_no_domain_change_was_needed: resolveEffectiveSettlement (packages/domain/src/outcomes/settlement-downstream.ts) already walks root -> tip via corrects_id and already refuses a broken chain. computeSettlementSummary already reports total_picks as the statistical contribution and total_records as 1 + correction_depth. So 'latest effective settlement wins' and 'one statistical contribution per pick' were already implemented and were simply unreachable from the evidence plane, because nothing ever wrote a corrects_id there. This was verified before the fix was written, and it is why the lane is typed runtime: packages/domain/src/** is not admitted by this lane type and did not need to be.

what_the_added_test_proves: Three operator grades on one real Track Only pick, submitted through submitPickController against real PostgREST, persist as THREE settlement_records rows — read back from the database ordered by created_at rather than from the return values.

Exactly ONE of the three has corrects_id IS NULL. That is the assertion the in-memory suite structurally cannot make: it is the live partial unique index settlement_records_pick_source_idx that permits the second and third rows only because they carry corrects_id, and a second canonical row would have been rejected by Postgres before the test could count it.

The chain is linked pairwise — grade 2's corrects_id is grade 1's id, grade 3's is grade 2's, NOT grade 1's — so a correction supersedes the current settlement rather than always pointing back at the original.
The original row still reads result='win' after two later grades. Immutability is measured in the database, not inferred from the absence of an UPDATE in the code.
The effective settlement is the tip (correction_depth 2, result 'win') and settlementSummary.total_picks is 1: three grades, one statistical contribution.
picks.status is still 'validated', zero pick_lifecycle rows carry to_state='settled', and distribution_outbox holds zero rows for the pick after all three grades.
runtime_proof.why_this_suite_and_not_the_in_memory_one: The in-memory repository does not enforce the (pick_id, source) partial unique index — packages/db/CLAUDE.md records this under Known Drift in as many words. So the in-memory tests can prove the chain is built correctly and cannot prove the database accepts it. Only the staging suite exercises the constraint that produced the original 23505.

directive_requirements.correction_creates_a_new_settlement_row: Asserted: three grades, three rows, distinct ids.
directive_requirements.corrects_id_references_the_superseded_se: Asserted pairwise rather than only at the tip, so 'always points at the original' would fail.
directive_requirements.latest_effective_settlement_wins: Asserted at every point in the chain, not only at the end: after grade N the effective result is grade N's result and correction_depth is N-1.
directive_requirements.23505_cannot_be_swallowed_and_returned_a: Asserted by the race test and mutation-verified by M2, which restores the old behaviour and turns exactly that test red.
directive_requirements.win_loss_win_produces_one_statistical_co: Asserted as settlementSummary.total_picks === 1 at each of the three points, alongside total_records === index + 1 so that 'the correction was recorded' is distinguished from 'the correction was double-counted'.

the_read_half_is_not_in_this_lane.finding: Four readers treat corrects_id IS NULL as 'the canonical settlement'. Once a correction exists that predicate selects the SUPERSEDED row, so a corrected pick would be reported with its old result. Sites: apps/command-center/src/lib/data/analytics.ts:317, :513, :773 and apps/api/src/model-performance-service.ts:184.
the_read_half_is_not_in_this_lane.is_this_a_regression_introduced_here: No. Those readers are wrong today and were unreachable today: nothing in the evidence plane ever wrote a corrects_id, so no correction existed for them to mis-select. This lane makes corrections possible, which is what makes the reader defect reachable — and fixing the writer first is the right order, because until a correction row exists there is nothing for those readers to select.
the_read_half_is_not_in_this_lane.why_it_is_not_in_this_lane: No lane type admits both surfaces. runtime admits apps/api/** and does not admit apps/command-center/**; delivery-ui admits apps/command-center/** and does not admit apps/api/**. Splitting the read half across two lanes, or re-typing this one to fit, are both worse than recording it.
the_read_half_is_not_in_this_lane.status: Recorded as the immediate follow-on lane. Not filed as new governance debt — it is product work with a named owner surface.
